title: Four turns to green
scenario: A platform team runs a coding agent on the Claude Agent SDK. You review one run that fixed a billing bug (exhibit). The team also asks you about a second job they plan to build next.
exhibit:
PROMPT: Fix the failing tests in billing.ts
OPTIONS: no max_turns, no max_budget_usd

turn 1  tool_use  Bash   bun test billing.test.ts
        result    2 failed, 14 passed
turn 2  tool_use  Read   billing.ts
        tool_use  Read   billing.test.ts
        result    file contents
turn 3  tool_use  Edit   billing.ts (round to cents)
        tool_use  Bash   bun test billing.test.ts
        result    0 failed, 16 passed
final   text      Fixed the rounding bug. All 16 tests pass.

RESULT  subtype: success

NEXT JOB (planned)
  every night: download sales.csv -> convert to JSON
  -> upload to the warehouse. Always these 3 steps.

questions.prompt: Why did the loop end after the final message?

options.text: The run hit its turn limit after three tool turns.
options.explanation: No `max_turns` was set, and the subtype is `success`. A turn limit would end with `error_max_turns`.

options.text: The SDK saw 0 failed tests and stopped the agent.
options.explanation: The SDK does not read test output. It only checks whether the model's response asks for more tools.

options.text: Claude produced a response with no tool calls.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say turns continue until Claude produces output with no tool calls; then the loop ends and the result is delivered.

options.text: The context window filled up and the SDK compacted it.
options.explanation: Compaction summarizes older history so the loop can go on. It does not end the loop.

questions.prompt: In turn 3, the agent runs the tests again after its edit. What does that give it?

options.text: Ground truth from the environment to check its progress.
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic engineering post says agents must gain ground truth from the environment at each step, such as tool call results or code execution.

options.text: A second turn budget, because test runs don't count as turns.
options.explanation: A Bash call is a tool call like any other. It is part of the turn it runs in.

options.text: Nothing new: the edit already proved the fix works.
options.explanation: An edit is an action, not a check. Only the new test output shows that the fix works.

options.text: A way to clear the old test output from the context.
options.explanation: The context does not reset between turns. The new output is added on top of the old one.

questions.prompt: The team now sets `max_turns` to 2 and runs the same prompt again. What happens, per the Claude docs?

options.text: Nothing changes: the final text reply happens anyway.
options.explanation: Turn 3 is a tool-use turn. With a limit of 2, the run never gets that far.

options.text: The run stops before the edit and ends with subtype `error_max_turns`.
options.explanation: Right. `max_turns` counts tool-use turns, and the docs' own example says a limit of 2 would stop before the edit step.

options.text: The run stops after turn 1, because each tool call counts as one turn.
options.explanation: A turn is one round trip, and it can hold several tool calls. Turn 2 has two reads and still counts once.

options.text: The run finishes, then reports `success` with a warning.
options.explanation: At the limit the loop stops early. The result subtype is `error_max_turns`, and it has no `result` text.

questions.prompt: For the planned nightly job, what does Anthropic's agents post suggest?

options.text: An agent, so the model can choose the order of the three steps.
options.explanation: The order never changes. Letting the model choose adds cost and a chance of errors with no gain.

options.text: An agent with a high turn limit, in case the upload fails.
options.explanation: A failed upload is a known case your code can retry. It does not need a model to direct the process.

options.text: Two agents, one to download and one to upload.
options.explanation: More agents add more cost. The post advises the simplest solution that works.

options.text: A workflow: the three steps run on a code path you write.
options.explanation: Right. Workflows orchestrate LLMs and tools through predefined code paths. Agents fit tasks where you can't hardcode a fixed path.
